answer: A reputation system that prices identity through work resists fake accounts: each agent must complete verifiable tasks before it can transact, and its standing is a prism that refracts every past interaction into one score — good behavior brightens it, cheating darkens it. New identities start with a sable, near-zero trust level, so an attacker who spawns a thousand clones faces an ocean of unpaid effort before any of them can move value. Forging one identity is cheap; forging a thousand trusted ones is not.
